page: Amazon Web Services c5a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by AMD EPYC 7R32 processors. The configuration features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 3.3 GHz. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio characteristic of compute-intensive infrastructure. The instance does not bundle local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote storage volumes, and offers a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight solid throughput across multi-threaded operations alongside moderate per-core processing metrics. In multi-core assessments, the system achieved a PassMark CPU score of 34,612.09 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 11,539.0, complemented by high-throughput software compilation metrics under Clang (22,726.0). Memory subsystems demonstrated strong performance, reflected in a PassMark memory score of 2,816.77 and large-block uncached read bandwidth of 73.17 GB/sec. However, single-core processing showed limitations, scoring 765.49 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the lower percentiles for pure single-thread intensity.

The CPU instruction set includes AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, but lacks AVX-512 extensions. The lack of hardware accelerators and bundled local disks presents a tradeoff that narrows its applicability for localized large storage caching or intensive matrix computing. Nevertheless, the high core count provides solid cost efficiency for parallelized processing jobs without paying a premium for memory-heavy configurations.
Amazon Web Services c5a.8xlarge is suited for distributed data processing, parallel build pipelines, CI/CD clusters, batch compute jobs, and medium-scale web application serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine operating on the Nitro hypervisor and driven by a 3.3 GHz AMD EPYC 7R32 processor. It supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory at 3 GHz, and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent state. Benchmark metrics reveal solid multi-core execution, demonstrated by 12,261.93 in multi-core stress-ng tests, a Clang compilation score of 22,726.0, and strong memory subsystem ratings, though single-core compute performance remains modest. Lacking AVX-512 extensions and dedicated GPU hardware, it optimizes resource allocation around high-density x86 parallel compute. The c5a.8xlarge serves well for CI/CD compilation pipelines, parallel batch processing, distributed data transformation, and horizontal web serving tiers.
